inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the visual / UX quality of the in-conference page (large video stage + toolbar + filmstrip).

EVIDENCE: Full-page screenshot of the conference page after a participant has joined and a remote video track is visible.

SCORE RANGE: 0-8 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. A large central video stage (or active-speaker tile) occupies the dominant portion of the viewport.
2. A bottom toolbar exposes at minimum: mute, camera, screen share, chat, hang up — clearly iconified.
3. A filmstrip (or tile view) shows other participants.
4. UI uses consistent spacing, colour, and typography (no raw-default browser controls).
5. Hover / focus affordances are visible on toolbar controls.
6. Critical state (muted indicator, active-speaker highlight) is visually clear.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Page does not render or shows raw HTML video controls.
- 2 (weak): Video shown but no toolbar or filmstrip.
- 5 (good): Stage + toolbar + filmstrip; visual polish uneven.
- 8 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied with a polished conference UI.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..8>, "reason": "<short justification citing visible markers>"}.

nodes.description: Architecture quality: registry-style Redux composition + feature modularity

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge whether the Redux store is composed via a registry-style pattern (lazy registration of reducers / middleware / listeners) and whether features are self-contained per-directory modules.

EVIDENCE: a `base/redux` (or equivalently named) folder exposing registry utilities, plus per-feature folders that wire themselves up on import. Concrete class names are NOT prescribed — accept any naming as long as the three responsibilities (reducer registration, middleware registration, listener / side-effect registration) are each handled by a dedicated utility.

SCORE RANGE: 0-8 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. There is a utility for registering reducers (one combined reducer for the whole store, but each feature plugs in its own slice).
2. There is a utility for registering middleware so feature modules add their own middleware without editing the root store.
3. There is a utility (or convention) for registering side-effect listeners (e.g. subscribe-and-react patterns) outside of reducers.
4. Each major feature (chat, video, recording, lobby, polls, av-moderation, …) is self-contained: its actions, action types, reducer, middleware, and components live under one directory.
5. Cross-feature communication happens exclusively via Redux actions / selectors — features do not import each other's internal helpers.
6. TypeScript (or JS-with-types) definitions exist for the Redux state and the action union.
7. The root store wires up the registries once at startup; feature modules do not call createStore directly.
8. Adding a new feature does not require modifying any existing feature's source.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Single combineReducers in the entry point; no registry pattern.
- 3 (weak): One registry-style utility exists; features still cross-import internals.
- 6 (good): All three registry-style utilities + feature modularity; some cross-imports remain.
- 8 (excellent): All eight criteria satisfied with idiomatic registry-based modularity.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..8>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

Architecture quality: clear separation between XMPP transport, signalling and business logic (stanza parse / route / action dispatch)

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the layering of XMPP message handling (connection / signaling / business-logic separation + connection state machine + recovery).

EVIDENCE: react/features/base/connection/* and react/features/base/conference/*, XMPP stanza handlers, connection-state action types.

SCORE RANGE: 0-6 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. There is an explicit connection layer responsible for transport (BOSH / WebSocket) and an upper signaling layer.
2. XMPP stanza parsing is decoupled from Redux action dispatch — handlers translate stanzas into typed actions before dispatching.
3. Connection state transitions are explicit (connecting -> connected -> disconnected) and represented in Redux state.
4. Reconnection / error-recovery paths exist (exponential backoff, lobby fallback, transport switch).
5. Business-logic features (chat, recording, polls) consume signaling events through Redux, not directly from XMPP.
6. Stanza handler registration is centralised so adding a new handler does not modify connection code.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): XMPP handlers dispatch business logic directly inline.
- 2 (weak): Some separation but connection state implicit; no recovery.
- 4 (good): Layered + state machine + Redux dispatch; recovery path thin.
- 6 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied with a clean XMPP architecture.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..6>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

nodes.description: Architecture quality: completeness of error handling and user feedback

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the error-handling and user-feedback design.

EVIDENCE: Notification system code, overlay / fallback components (PageReloadOverlay, etc.), i18n strings for errors.

SCORE RANGE: 0-5 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Network or XMPP errors trigger a user-visible notification (no white screen).
2. Errors are categorised at least into fatal / recoverable / info with consistent UI treatment.
3. Mid-conference disconnects show a reconnect / retry overlay (e.g. PageReloadOverlay, ReloadTimer).
4. Error messages go through the i18n layer (no hard-coded English strings).
5. Critical degradations (microphone permission denied, camera busy) include a remedy hint, not just an error code.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Errors silently logged or cause a blank page.
- 1 (very weak): Notifications exist for some errors only.
- 3 (acceptable): Categorisation + reload overlay; i18n thin.
- 5 (excellent): All five criteria satisfied with comprehensive error UX.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..5>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

nodes.description: Architecture quality: regularity and consistency of Redux state management

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the regularity and consistency of Redux state management.

EVIDENCE: Per-feature actionTypes / actions / reducer files; persisted-subset configuration; subscribe-and-react side-effect handling; async action creators.

SCORE RANGE: 0-6 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Each feature has a clean three-file split (actionTypes / actions / reducer) — file extension can be .ts or .js.
2. A curated subset of state is persisted (e.g. user settings) — not the whole store. The mechanism (registry helper, redux-persist whitelist, custom middleware …) is up to the candidate.
3. Side effects (subscriptions, transports, browser APIs) live in dedicated subscribe-and-react helpers, not inside reducers.
4. Async actions use thunks (or equivalent middleware) so reducers stay pure.
5. State shape is normalised — no arbitrarily deep nesting; collections keyed by id.
6. Selectors are colocated with their feature and accept the root state for testability.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Reducers contain side effects; no actionTypes file; no thunks.
- 2 (weak): Some features use the three-file split; persistence ad hoc.
- 4 (good): Three-file + thunks + listener-based side effects; normalisation thin.
- 6 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied with idiomatic Redux usage.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..6>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

nodes.description: Architecture quality: WebRTC media-pipeline design (track lifecycle, P2P/SFU switch, codec negotiation)

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the WebRTC media-pipeline design (track lifecycle, P2P/SFU switch, codec preference, screen share, processors).

EVIDENCE: react/features/base/tracks/* (or equivalent), conference media setup, codec preference config, MediaProcessor / streamEffects code.

SCORE RANGE: 0-6 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Track creation / disposal is managed via Redux actions (TRACK_ADDED / TRACK_REMOVED) — components don't handle MediaStreamTracks directly.
2. P2P -> SFU (and back) mode switch is implemented when participant count crosses a threshold.
3. Codec preference (e.g. AV1 > VP9 > VP8 > H264) is configurable through config.js.
4. Screen share is modelled as its own track type, distinct from camera.
5. Virtual background / noise suppression are implemented as MediaProcessor pipeline steps that can be chained.
6. Track muting / unmuting yields events consumed by other features (UI, recording, statistics).

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Tracks are managed inline in components; no pipeline.
- 2 (weak): Redux track lifecycle but no P2P/SFU switch and no processors.
- 4 (good): Lifecycle + screen share + codec preference; processors thin.
- 6 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied with a complete media pipeline.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..6>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

nodes.description: UI quality: accessibility - ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus management

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge accessibility (ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus management, shortcuts, contrast).

EVIDENCE: Toolbar / dialog component code, keyboard-handler utilities, theme / colour tokens.

SCORE RANGE: 0-5 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Toolbar buttons carry aria-label attributes describing their action.
2. Dialogs use role='dialog' with aria-modal='true' and aria-labelledby pointing to a title node.
3. Focus is trapped inside open dialogs and restored on close.
4. Keyboard shortcuts (e.g. M = mute, C = chat, R = raise hand) are implemented and discoverable.
5. Colour contrast for text and focus rings meets WCAG AA (>= 4.5:1 for body text).

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): No ARIA labels and no keyboard shortcuts.
- 1 (very weak): Sparse aria-label on a few buttons.
- 3 (acceptable): ARIA + dialogs + focus trap; shortcuts and contrast thin.
- 5 (excellent): All five criteria satisfied with strong accessibility.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..5>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

nodes.description: UI quality: responsive layout - adaptive behaviour across screen sizes

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the responsive-layout design (window-resize handling, filmstrip orientation, tile auto-grid, toolbar overflow).

EVIDENCE: react/features/base/responsive-ui/*, filmstrip and tile-view components, toolbar overflow component, CSS / SCSS breakpoints.

SCORE RANGE: 0-6 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. A responsive-ui feature listens for window resize and updates layout dimensions in Redux.
2. Filmstrip switches between horizontal / vertical orientations based on aspect ratio or width.
3. Tile View computes rows/cols dynamically from participant count to maximise tile size.
4. The toolbar collapses surplus actions into an overflow menu at narrow widths.
5. CSS media queries (or JS breakpoints) implement at least three responsive breakpoints (mobile / tablet / desktop).
6. Screen resizing during a call does not cause layout flicker or stale tile counts.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Fixed-width layout; resizing breaks the page.
- 2 (weak): Some media queries but filmstrip / tile not adaptive.
- 4 (good): Filmstrip + tile auto-grid + breakpoints; toolbar overflow thin.
- 6 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied with full responsive coverage.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..6>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.
